pages.title: System, Boundary, and Surroundings
pages.description: Defines thermodynamic systems, boundaries, surroundings, and common system classifications.

pages.title: Properties, States, and Equilibrium
pages.description: Introduces thermodynamic properties, states, equilibrium, and the state postulate.

pages.title: Thermodynamic Processes and Cycles
pages.description: Explains processes, paths, cycles, and changes between thermodynamic states.

pages.title: Heat and Work Interactions
pages.description: Distinguishes heat and work as energy interactions across a system boundary.

pages.title: Pure Substances, Phases, and Property Diagrams
pages.description: Introduces pure substances, phase behavior, saturation, and thermodynamic property diagrams.

pages.title: Property Model and Table Selection
pages.description: Guides the selection of appropriate property models, tables, and equations of state.

pages.title: Thermodynamic Assumptions and Model Reduction
pages.description: Shows how assumptions simplify thermodynamic models while preserving physically meaningful behavior.

pages.title: Purpose of the Second Law and Energy Quality
pages.description: Explains why the Second Law is needed and distinguishes energy quantity from energy quality.

pages.title: Thermal Energy Reservoirs
pages.description: Defines thermal energy reservoirs and their roles in cyclic thermal devices.

pages.title: Heat Engines and Thermal Efficiency
pages.description: Describes heat-engine energy flows and evaluates performance using thermal efficiency.

pages.title: Refrigerators, Heat Pumps, and COP
pages.description: Compares refrigerators and heat pumps and defines their coefficients of performance.

pages.title: Reversibility, Irreversibility, and Carnot Limits
pages.description: Introduces reversible processes, irreversibility, and ideal Carnot performance limits.
